citation: Yuan H, Ma X, Xu J, Han P, Rao G, Chen G, Zhang K, Yang R, Han C, Jiang M. Application of metagenomic next-generation sequencing in the clinical diagnosis of infectious diseases after allo-HSCT: a single-center analysis. BMC Infectious Diseases. 2024;24:452.
study_design: Retrospective single-center analysis (patients enrolled and tested Oct 2019 - Feb 2022; no prospective enrollment described)

population.population_description: Patients with fever of unknown origin after allo-HSCT (>7 days, axillary temperature >38 C, on immunosuppressants and/or anti-infective therapy) at First Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University

neutropenic_status: Not defined/reported as a criterion; immunosuppressant use and persistent fever >7 days were the inclusion criteria

index_test.platform_or_panel: In-house metagenomic next-generation sequencing, DNA only (fastp/Komplexity filtering; previously described pipeline [ref 16])
index_test.dna_and_or_rna: DNA only ("only DNA was sequenced by mNGS and any RNA viruses would likely not be detected")

reference_standard: Clinical diagnosis based on diagnostic criteria for infection after HSCT: mNGS result, CMTs, imaging, clinical manifestations; final classification made clinically (46 infectious, 8 non-infectious incl. interstitial pneumonia/bronchiolitis obliterans)

comparator_2x2.against: conventional microbiological tests (CMTs), Table 2, n=54 patients/initial samples
comparator_2x2.note: This is agreement with CMT, NOT against the final clinical diagnosis; final-diagnosis 2x2 not reported. Positive rates: mNGS 88.9% vs CMT 33.3%.

diagnostic_yield.n_positive_relevant_pathogens: 46 cases of infectious diseases diagnosed (22 viral, 13 fungal, 11 bacterial)
diagnostic_yield.yield_percent: 88.9% positive detection rate of mNGS (vs 33.3% CMT)
diagnostic_yield.basis: positive mNGS tests among 54 patients initially tested; 46/54 (85.2%) had infectious disease diagnosis

additional_yield_vs_conventional: Of 54 patients, 31 were mNGS-positive/CMT-negative, 17 both positive, 1 CMT-positive/mNGS-negative, 5 both negative (Table 2). 41 pathogens identified by both mNGS and CMTs.
therapy_change: Among 46 cases diagnosed by mNGS, 43 patients modified their treatment plans and experienced positive outcomes.
mortality_or_outcomes: Two patients died from recurrent infection with fungi and drug-resistant bacteria after transplantation (Table 3); three cases resulted in fatalities due to severe bacterial bloodstream infections (2 Klebsiella pneumoniae, 1 Pseudomonas aeruginosa).

quality_flags.overlap_risk: Single center, same patients contribute initial and repeat mNGS tests (7 patients re-tested); 61 tests in 54 patients

quadas2_notes: Retrospective single-center; no consecutive/prospective enrollment stated; final clinical diagnosis incorporates mNGS results (incorporation/circularity risk for accuracy estimates); 2x2 available only vs CMT (Table 2), not vs final diagnosis; TAT not reported.

evidence_quotes.claim: n=54 febrile allo-HSCT patients, study period
evidence_quotes.quote: Fifty-four patients who had fever following allo-HSCT from October 2019 to February 2022 were enrolled.
A total of 61 mNGS tests were performed, resulting in the diagnosis of 46 cases of infectious diseases.
The positive detection rates of mNGS and CMT were 88.9% and 33.3%, respectively, with significant differences
Regarding the initial examination samples of the 54 patients, peripheral blood was the most commonly collected (39 cases, 72.2%), followed by BALF (13 cases, 24.1%), and CSF (2 cases, 3.7%).

For patients with an undetermined pathogen, mNGS was performed on the DNA samples only.
Among 46 cases of patients with infectious diseases diagnosed by mNGS, 43 patients modified their treatment plans and experienced positive outcomes.
Two patients died from recurrent infection with fungi and drug-resistant bacteria after transplantation
According to clinical and microbiological diagnosis, 46 cases (46/54, 85.2%) were determined to have infectious diseases
A total of 41 pathogens were identified by both mNGS and CMTs

exclusion_reason: No 2x2 against final clinical diagnosis; only mNGS-vs-CMT agreement reported; final diagnosis incorporates mNGS (circularity).
